2.6 Gaps and Future Work in Existing Research 
Despite significant research into educational frameworks and technologies, there 
are still gaps in the existing body of research and current solutions. 
Although certain applications integrating education frameworks such as Duolingo 
and RemNote; there is limited research on the actual effects of these 
frameworks within eLearning applications. Individual frameworks and 
technologies such as AR, AI, and microlearning show promise, however, they are 
often studied in isolation. Future solutions should aim to use frameworks and 
technologies in combination and cater to a diverse range of student learning 
needs. 
Current research hints towards the potential positive impact of personalised and 
adaptive learning tools. However, there seems to be limited research into 
systems that change content and difficulty based on real-time student 
performance. 
Although microlearning and gamification are shown to increase student 
engagement and retention. The long-term impacts on deep learning and true 
mastery of a subject are unknown. Future research should investigate the 
effects of these strategies over the long-term on student understanding, and 
identify how it may be optimised. 
There is limited research looking into a quantitative analysis of learning-out 
comes using short-form content especially across different subjects. Particularly 
between subjects that require repeated practice, like mathematics, and more 
memorisation intensive subjects like biology.
